cards.title: Introduction to Vue.js
cards.content:
Vue.js is a progressive JavaScript framework used for building user interfaces and single-page applications.

It focuses on the view layer and is easily integrable with other libraries or existing projects.

options.text: A progressive JavaScript framework for building UIs

content.text: To create a new Vue application instance, we use the function createApp imported from the 'vue' package.

cards.title: Reactivity in Vue 3
cards.content:
Vue 3 introduces the Composition API, where we use the ref() or reactive() functions to declare reactive state.

import { ref } from 'vue';

const count = ref(0);

cards.title: Computed Properties vs Methods
cards.content:
Computed properties are cached based on their reactive dependencies. They only re-evaluate when some of their reactive dependencies have changed.

const doubleCount = computed(() => count.value * 2);

options.text: They always re-run on every re-render regardless of changes.
They are cached based on their reactive dependencies.

cards.title: Components and Props
cards.content: Components are reusable Vue instances with a name. Props are custom attributes you can register on a component to pass data down from parent to child.

cards.title: Summary of Vue Fundamentals
cards.content: You have covered the core concepts of Vue.js: the instance, reactivity with Composition API, directives, lifecycle hooks, computed properties, and components.
